t: You're at All Saints' Church, the ancient parish church of Fulham, standing close to the Thames beside the northern approach to Putney Bridge. It began as the parish church of the Bishops of London, who held the neighbouring Fulham Manor from the eighth century, and several of them are buried here. They include Henry Compton, John Robinson, Edmund Gibson, Thomas Sherlock, Charles James Blomfield and Robert Lowth, who also wrote one of the most influential English grammar textbooks. The tower, nave and chancel are Grade Two star listed.
